sanskrit: sa vānaramahārājaḥ śayānaḥ śaravikṣataḥ pratyukto hetumadvākyair nottaraṃ pratyapadyata
english: That great king of the monkeys, struck by the arrow and lying prostrate, though addressed with reasoned words, could find no reply.

sanskrit: aśmabhiḥ paribhinnāṅgaḥ pādapair āhato bhṛśam rāmabāṇena cākrānto jīvitānte mumoha saḥ
english: His limbs shattered by rocks, grievously struck by trees, and now overwhelmed by Rāma's arrow, he fell into a swoon at the threshold of death.

sanskrit: taṃ bhāryābāṇamokṣeṇa rāmadattena saṃyuge hataṃ plavagaśārdūlaṃ tārā śuśrāva vālinam
english: Tārā heard that Vālin, that tiger among monkeys and her own lord, had been slain in battle by the arrow discharged by Rāma at a wife's behest.

sanskrit: sā saputrāpriyaṃ śrutvā vadhaṃ bhartuḥ sudāruṇam niṣpapāta bhṛśaṃ trastā vividhād girigahvarāt
english: Hearing that most terrible news of her husband's death — dreadful alike for her and for her son — she rushed out in great terror from the various mountain caves.

sanskrit: ye tv aṅgadaparīvārā vānarā hi mahābalāḥ te sakārmukam ālokya rāmaṃ trastāḥ pradudruvuḥ
english: The mighty monkeys who formed Aṅgada's escort, catching sight of Rāma with his bow, fled in terror.

sanskrit: sā dadarśa tatas trastān harīn āpatato drutam yūthād iva paribhraṣṭān mṛgān nihatayūthapān
english: She then saw the terrified monkeys racing toward her in headlong flight — like deer scattered from a herd whose leader has been slain.

sanskrit: tān uvāca samāsādya duḥkhitān duḥkhitā satī rāma vitrāsitān sarvān anubaddhān iveṣubhiḥ
english: She, herself stricken with grief, approached those grief-stricken ones — all of them put to flight by Rāma as though pursued by his arrows — and spoke to them.

sanskrit: vānarā rājasiṃhasya yasya yūyaṃ puraḥsarāḥ taṃ vihāya suvitrastāḥ kasmād dravata durgatāḥ
english: "O monkeys, you who were the vanguard of that lion among kings — why do you flee in such great terror, abandoning him, reduced to this miserable state?"

sanskrit: rājyahetoḥ sa ced bhrātā bhrātā raudreṇa pātitaḥ rāmeṇa prasṛtair dūrān mārgaṇair dūra pātibhiḥ
english: "If indeed that brother has felled this brother for the sake of a kingdom — by Rāma, with his far-flying shafts loosed from a distance — then flee!"

sanskrit: kapipatnyā vacaḥ śrutvā kapayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ prāptakālam aviśliṣṭam ūcur vacanam aṅganām
english: Hearing the words of the monkey-queen, the monkeys — those shape-shifters — spoke to her in timely and coherent words.

sanskrit: jīva putre nivartasya putraṃ rakṣasva cāndagam antako rāma rūpeṇa hatvā nayati vālinam
english: "Live for your son — turn back! Protect your son Aṅgada. Death, having taken the form of Rāma, has slain Vālin and carries him away."

sanskrit: kṣiptān vṛkṣān samāvidhya vipulāś ca śilās tathā vālī vajrasamair bāṇair vajreṇeva nipātitaḥ
english: "Vālin, who had hurled uprooted trees and massive boulders — that Vālin has been struck down by arrows like thunderbolts, as if by the thunderbolt itself."

sanskrit: abhidrutam idaṃ sarvaṃ vidrutaṃ prasṛtaṃ balam asmin plavagaśārdūle hate śakrasamaprabhe
english: "With this tiger among monkeys slain — he whose splendor was equal to Indra's — this entire army that had charged forward has now scattered and fled."

sanskrit: rakṣyatāṃ nagaraṃ śūrair aṅgadaś cābhiṣicyatām padasthaṃ vālinaḥ putraṃ bhajiṣyanti plavaṃgamāḥ
english: "Let the city be guarded by the heroes, and let Aṅgada be consecrated as king. Standing firm in his father's place, the monkeys will rally to Vālin's son."

sanskrit: atha vā ruciraṃ sthānam iha te rucirānane āviśanti hi durgāṇi kṣipram adyaiva vānarāḥ
english: "Or else, O fair-faced one, this stronghold is a fitting refuge for you — the monkeys are quickly entering the fortresses even today."

sanskrit: abhāryāḥ saha bhāryāś ca santy atra vanacāriṇaḥ lubdhebhyo viprayuktebhyaḥ svebhyo nas tumulaṃ bhayam
english: "Among these forest-dwellers, some have wives and some do not; we face tremendous danger from our own folk — the greedy and the lawless."

sanskrit: alpāntaragatānāṃ tu śrutvā vacanam aṅganā ātmanaḥ pratirūpaṃ sā babhāṣe cāruhāsinī
english: Having heard the words of those who had drawn near within a short distance, that beautiful-smiling woman spoke what was fitting for herself.

sanskrit: putreṇa mama kiṃ kāryaṃ kiṃ rājyena kim ātmanā kapisiṃhe mahābhāge tasmin bhartari naśyati
english: "What need have I of a son, what of a kingdom, what of my own life, now that that most glorious lion among monkeys, my husband, has perished?"

sanskrit: pādamūlaṃ gamiṣyāmi tasyaivāhaṃ mahātmanaḥ yo 'sau rāmaprayuktena śareṇa vinipātitaḥ
english: "I shall go to the feet of that noble great-souled one himself, who has been struck down by the arrow set flying by Rāma."

sanskrit: evam uktvā pradudrāva rudatī śokakarśitā śiraś coraś ca bāhubhyāṃ duḥkhena samabhighnatī
english: Having spoken thus, she ran forward weeping, wasted by grief, beating her head and her breast with her arms in her anguish.

sanskrit: āvrajantī dadarśātha patiṃ nipatitaṃ bhuvi hantāraṃ dānavendrāṇāṃ samareṣv anivartinām
english: As she hurried forward she then saw her husband fallen upon the ground — he who in battles had never turned back, the slayer of lords of demons.

sanskrit: kṣeptāraṃ parvatendrāṇāṃ vajrāṇām iva vāsavam mahāvātasamāviṣṭaṃ mahāmeghaughaniḥsvanam
english: He who had hurled the kings of mountains like Vāsava his thunderbolts, who had been filled with the force of a great storm and roared like a mass of great thunder-clouds —

sanskrit: śakratulyaparākrāntaṃ vṛṣṭvevoparataṃ ghanam nardantaṃ nardatāṃ bhīmaṃ śūraṃ śūreṇa pātitam
english: — whose valor equaled Indra's, terrible in his roaring among those who roar, like a cloud stilled after releasing its rain, that hero laid low by a hero.

sanskrit: śārdūlenāmiṣasyārthe mṛgarājaṃ yathā hatam arcitaṃ sarvalokasya sapatākaṃ savedikam
english: As a tiger kills a lion for the sake of flesh — him who was honored by all the world with banners and ceremonial platforms.

sanskrit: nāgahetoḥ suparṇena caityam unmathitaṃ yathā avaṣṭabhyāvatiṣṭhantaṃ dadarśa dhanur ūrjitam
english: As Garuḍa demolishes a sacred tree for the sake of a serpent — thus she saw him, still grasping and upholding his mighty bow, even as he lay fallen.

sanskrit: rāmaṃ rāmānujaṃ caiva bhartuś caivānujaṃ śubhā tān atītya samāsādya bhartāraṃ nihataṃ raṇe
english: That beautiful woman passed by Rāma and Rāma's younger brother, and also her husband's younger brother, and drew near to her husband slain in battle.

sanskrit: samīkṣya vyathitā bhūmau saṃbhrāntā nipapāta ha supteva punar utthāya āryaputreti krośatī
english: Gazing upon him she fell to the ground, anguished and bewildered; then rising again as if from sleep, she cried aloud, "My noble lord!"

sanskrit: ruroda sā patiṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃditaṃ mṛtyudāmabhiḥ tām avekṣya tu sugrīvaḥ krośantīṃ kurarīm iva
english: She wept, beholding her husband bound fast in the bonds of death. Sugrīva, watching her crying out like an osprey, —

sanskrit: viṣādam agamat kaṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā cāṅgadam āgatam
english: — fell into deep despondency, and seeing Aṅgada also arrived, sorrow overwhelmed him.

sanskrit: rāmacāpavisṛṣṭena śareṇāntakareṇa tam dṛṣṭvā vinihataṃ bhūmau tārā tārādhipānanā
english: Tārā — she whose face was like the lord of stars — seeing him struck down upon the ground by the death-dealing arrow loosed from Rāma's bow,

sanskrit: sā samāsādya bhartāraṃ paryaṣvajata bhāminī iṣuṇābhihataṃ dṛṣṭvā vālinaṃ kuñjaropamam
english: that passionate woman drew near to her husband and embraced him, seeing Vālin, who resembled a great elephant, struck down by the shaft.

sanskrit: vānarendraṃ mahendrābhaṃ śokasaṃtaptamānasā tārā tarum ivonmūlaṃ paryadevayad āturā
english: Tārā lamented in anguish over the lord of monkeys, who resembled great Indra, her heart tormented by grief — as over a great tree torn up by the roots.

sanskrit: raṇe dāruṇavikrānta pravīra plavatāṃ vara kiṃ dīnām apurobhāgām adya tvaṃ nābhibhāṣase
english: "O you of terrible valor in battle, O hero, O best among those who leap — why do you not speak today to me who am wretched and without good fortune?"

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha hariśārdūla bhajasva śayanottamam naivaṃvidhāḥ śerate hi bhūmau nṛpatisattamāḥ
english: "Rise, O tiger among monkeys, and take your place on an excellent couch — for kings of your kind do not lie upon the bare earth."

sanskrit: atīva khalu te kāntā vasudhā vasudhādhipa gatāsur api yāṃ gātrair māṃ vihāya niṣevase
english: "Truly the earth is exceedingly dear to you, O lord of the earth, that even having lost your breath of life you abandon me and lie embracing her with your limbs."

sanskrit: vyaktam anyā tvayā vīra dharmataḥ saṃpravartatā kiṣkindheva purī ramyā svargamārge vinirmitā
english: "It is clear, O hero, that another has been chosen by you, you who proceed according to your own dharma — a beautiful city like Kiṣkindhā has been fashioned for you on the path to heaven."

sanskrit: yāny asmābhis tvayā sārdhaṃ vaneṣu madhugandhiṣu vihṛtāni tvayā kāle teṣām uparamaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "Those pleasures we enjoyed together with you in the fragrant forests — you have in your time put an end to all of them."

sanskrit: nirānandā nirāśāhaṃ nimagnā śokasāgare tvayi pañcatvam āpanne mahāyūthapayūthape
english: "I am joyless, I am hopeless, plunged into an ocean of grief, now that you — the lord of great monkey-troops — have been reduced to the five elements."

sanskrit: hṛdayaṃ susthiraṃ mahyaṃ dṛṣṭvā vinihataṃ bhuvi yan na śokābhisaṃtaptaṃ sphuṭate 'dya sahasradhā
english: "My heart is very firm indeed — that, seeing you struck down upon the ground, it does not burst today into a thousand pieces, scorched by grief."

sanskrit: sugrīvasya tvayā bhāryā hṛtā sa ca vivāsitaḥ yat tat tasya tvayā vyuṣṭiḥ prāpteyaṃ plavagādhipa
english: "You seized Sugrīva's wife and drove him into exile — and now, O lord of monkeys, this retribution from him has come upon you for that deed."

sanskrit: niḥśreyasaparā mohāt tvayā cāhaṃ vigarhitā yaiṣābruvaṃ hitaṃ vākyaṃ vānarendrahitaiṣiṇī
english: "And I too, who out of concern for the welfare of the lord of monkeys had spoken words of benefit to you, was censured by you in delusion as one fixated on mokṣa."

sanskrit: kālo niḥsaṃśayo nūnaṃ jīvitāntakaras tava balād yenāvapanno 'si sugrīvasyāvaśo vaśam
english: "Time, the ender of life, is doubtless irresistible — it is by Time's force that you have fallen helplessly under Sugrīva's power."

sanskrit: vaidhavyaṃ śokasaṃtāpaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ kṛpaṇā satī aduḥkhopacitā pūrvaṃ vartayiṣyāmy anāthavat
english: "Wretched that I am, a wretched woman, unaccustomed to sorrow before, I shall now live out widowhood, grief, and torment, like one without a protector."

sanskrit: lālitaś cāṅgado vīraḥ sukumāraḥ sukhocitaḥ vatsyate kām avasthāṃ me pitṛvye krodhamūrchite
english: "Aṅgada the hero, who was pampered, tender, accustomed to comfort — in what condition will he live now for me, with his uncle enraged and maddened?"

sanskrit: kuruṣva pitaraṃ putra sudṛṣṭaṃ dharmavatsalam durlabhaṃ darśanaṃ tv asya tava vatsa bhaviṣyati
english: "Look well upon your father, my son — he who was devoted to dharma and virtuous. The sight of him, my dear child, will henceforth be hard to obtain."

sanskrit: samāśvāsaya putraṃ tvaṃ saṃdeśaṃ saṃdiśasva ca mūrdhni cainaṃ samāghrāya pravāsaṃ prasthito hy asi
english: "Comfort your son, and give him your final message; sniff his head in farewell, for you are departing on a long journey from which there is no return."

sanskrit: rāmeṇa hi mahat karma kṛtaṃ tvām abhinighnatā ānṛṇyaṃ tu gataṃ tasya sugrīvasya pratiśrave
english: "Great indeed is the deed done by Rāma in slaying you — he has thereby discharged his debt in fulfillment of his pledge to Sugrīva."

sanskrit: sakāmo bhava sugrīva rumāṃ tvaṃ pratipatsyase bhuṅkṣva rājyam anudvignaḥ śasto bhrātā ripus tava
english: "May you have your desire, Sugrīva — you shall recover Rumā; rule the kingdom without anxiety; your enemy, your brother, has been slain."

sanskrit: kiṃ mām evaṃ vilapatīṃ preṃṇā tvaṃ nābhibhāṣase imāḥ paśya varā bahvīr bhāryās te vānareśvara
english: "Why do you not speak to me with affection as I lament so? Look upon these, your many excellent wives, O lord of monkeys."

sanskrit: tasyā vilapitaṃ śrutvā vānaryaḥ sarvataś ca tāḥ parigṛhyāṅgadaṃ dīnaṃ duḥkhārtāḥ paricukruśuḥ
english: Hearing her lament, the female monkeys all around, embracing the wretched Aṅgada, cried out in their anguish.

sanskrit: kim aṅgadaṃ sāṅgada vīra bāho vihāya yāsy adya cirapravāsaṃ na yuktam evaṃ guṇasaṃnikṛṣṭaṃ vihāya putraṃ priyaputra gantum
english: "O hero of powerful arms, why do you depart today on this long journey leaving Aṅgada behind? It is not fitting, O you who loved your son, to go thus, leaving behind a son so close to you in virtues."

sanskrit: kim apriyaṃ te priyacāruveṣa kṛtaṃ mayā nātha sutena vā te sahāyinīm adya vihāya vīra yamakṣayaṃ gacchasi durvinītam
english: "What wrong have I done you, O master of lovely and pleasing form, or what has your son done, that today, O hero, leaving me your companion, you go recklessly to the abode of Yama?"

sanskrit: yady apriyaṃ kiṃ cid asaṃpradhārya kṛtaṃ mayā syāt tava dīrghabāho kṣamasva me tad dharivaṃśa nātha vrajāmi mūrdhnā tava vīra pādau
english: "If I have done anything displeasing to you without knowing it, forgive me for that, O long-armed one, O master of the monkey lineage — I go, O hero, touching your feet with my head."

sanskrit: tathā tu tārā karuṇaṃ rudantī bhartuḥ samīpe saha vānarībhiḥ vyavasyata prāyam anindyavarṇā upopaveṣṭuṃ bhuvi yatra vālī
english: And thus Tārā, of blameless complexion, weeping piteously together with the female monkeys near her husband, resolved upon the fast unto death, settling down beside Vālin where he lay upon the ground.

sanskrit: tato nipatitāṃ tārāṃ cyutāṃ tārām ivāmbarāt śanair āśvāsayām āsa hanūmān hariyūthapaḥ
english: Then Hanūmān, the leader of the monkey troops, gently consoled Tārā where she had fallen — like a star fallen from the sky.

sanskrit: guṇadoṣakṛtaṃ jantuḥ svakarmaphalahetukam avyagras tad avāpnoti sarvaṃ pretya śubhāśubham
english: "A being, composed of virtues and faults, and conditioned by the fruits of its own actions, receives without fail all the good and ill that is due to it in the next world."

sanskrit: śocyā śocasi kaṃ śocyaṃ dīnaṃ dīnānukampase kaś ca kasyānuśocyo 'sti dehe 'smin budbudopame
english: "You who are worthy of lamentation lament for whom? You who are pitiable take pity on whom who is pitiable? And who is there to mourn for whom, in this body that is like a bubble?"

sanskrit: aṅgadas tu kumāro 'yaṃ draṣṭavyo jīvaputrayā āyatyā ca vidheyāni samarthāny asya cintaya
english: "This prince Aṅgada must be looked after by you who have a son still living; think also of what is capable of being done for him in the future."

sanskrit: jānāsy aniyatām evaṃ bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim tasmāc chubhaṃ hi kartavyaṃ paṇḍite naihalaukikam
english: "You know that the coming and going of all beings is thus uncertain; therefore, O wise one, what is auspicious must be done — not what is merely of this world."

sanskrit: yasmin harisahasrāṇi prayutāny arbudāni ca vartayanti kṛtāṃśāni so 'yaṃ diṣṭāntam āgataḥ
english: "He in whose service thousands, millions, and ten-hundreds-of-millions of monkeys performed their appointed portions — even he has come to his fated end."

sanskrit: yad ayaṃ nyāyadṛṣṭārthaḥ sāmadānakṣamāparaḥ gato dharmajitāṃ bhūmiṃ nainaṃ śocitum arhasi
english: "Because he was one who perceived things rightly, who was devoted to conciliation, generosity, and forbearance, he has gone to the realm won by dharma — you ought not to grieve for him."

sanskrit: sarve ca hariśārdūla putraś cāyaṃ tavāṅgadaḥ haryṛṣkapatirājyaṃ ca tvatsanātham anindite
english: "All the monkeys, and this your son Aṅgada, and the kingdom of the lords of monkeys and bears — all these, O blameless one, have you as their protector."

sanskrit: tāv imau śokasaṃtaptau śanaiḥ preraya bhāmini tvayā parigṛhīto 'yam aṅgadaḥ śāstu medinīm
english: "Gently urge these two who are tormented by grief, O passionate one; let this Aṅgada, taken under your guardianship, rule the earth."

sanskrit: saṃtatiś ca yathādṛṣṭā kṛtyaṃ yac cāpi sāmpratam rājñas tat kriyatāṃ sarvam eṣa kālasya niścayaḥ
english: "And the line of succession as it has been established, and whatever is now the pressing duty for the king — let all of that be carried out; such is Time's decree."

sanskrit: saṃskāryo harirājas tu aṅgadaś cābhiṣicyatām siṃhāsanagataṃ putraṃ paśyantī śāntim eṣyasi
english: "Let the king of monkeys be duly cremated, and let Aṅgada be consecrated; beholding your son seated upon the lion-throne, you will find peace."

sanskrit: sā tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā bhartṛvyasanapīḍitā abravīd uttaraṃ tārā hanūmantam avasthitam
english: She, tormented by the calamity of losing her husband, heard his words and replied to Hanūmān as he stood before her.

sanskrit: aṅgada pratirūpāṇāṃ putrāṇām ekataḥ śatam hatasyāpy asya vīrasya gātrasaṃśleṣaṇaṃ varam
english: "A hundred sons equal to Aṅgada placed on one side — the embrace of the body of this hero, even slain, is better."

sanskrit: na cāhaṃ harirājasya prabhavāmy aṅgadasya vā pitṛvyastasya sugrīvaḥ sarvakāryeṣv anantaraḥ
english: "And I have no power over the kingdom of the monkey king, nor over Aṅgada — Sugrīva, his paternal uncle, is the next in authority in all matters."

sanskrit: na hy eṣā buddhir āstheyā hanūmann aṅgadaṃ prati pitā hi bandhuḥ putrasya na mātā harisattama
english: "This resolve is not to be entertained regarding Aṅgada, O Hanūmān — for it is the father who is the kinsman of the son, not the mother, O best of monkeys."

sanskrit: na hi mama harirājasaṃśrayāt kṣamataram asti paratra ceha vā abhimukhahatavīrasevitaṃ śayanam idaṃ mama sevituṃ kṣamam
english: "For there is nothing more fitting for me than to take refuge with the king of monkeys — in this world or the next; and it is fitting that I attend upon this couch attended by the hero who fell facing the foe."
